newsitem.title: UK: Euro veg oils little changed despite U.S. 4 yr low.
newsitem.headline: Euro veg oils little changed despite U.S. 4 yr low.

text.p: European vegetable oil prices were little changed on Tuesday morning despite the four year low in Chicago soy oil futures at the close on Monday.
Currency and south American stocks dominated the European market.
Traders said the sharp fall in Chicago was an over-reaction by longs to the USDA crop report which was not reflected in the physical market.

"The old crop carryover was down again, but people here are also looking at South America which has never been sold so far forward at this time of year before and there is some concern over stocks there," said one trader.
Traders said the strong dollar was also a factor with crushers finding their margins squeezed.
"Crushers are having a job finding a margin with the dollar so strong, and they are calling the tune, not Chicago," said another trader.
At the opening Dutch soy oil was unchanged to 0.50 guilders down while rape oil was 0.50 guilders higher.
Opening crude palm oil offers were not down as much as expected following a wave of refiner buying in Malaysian towards the close.
"One major player has been buying, what we don't know is whether they are covering positions or just trying to support the market," said a trader.
Crude palm oil cif Europe opened $2.50 down to unchanged after Jul and Aug both traded at $512.50 a tonne cif Europe before the Malaysian market turned higher towards the close.
Lauric oils were mixed with coconut oil $2.50 down to unchanged and palmkernel oil $2.50 to $7.50 up, but again there was little sign of buyers.
